classifications.rationale: The President states a substantive eligibility condition for Mexican steel imports: duty-free treatment is available only when the steel is melted and poured in Mexico, Canada, or the United States. That legal eligibility consequence is stated in the segment itself, notwithstanding its additional monitoring and advisory directions.
classifications.evidence: In order to be eligible for importation free from section 232 tariffs, steel articles and derivative steel articles that are products of Mexico must be melted and poured in Mexico, Canada, or the United States.

classifications.rationale: The President presently determines that the existing tariff level for other countries will remain in force; the legal consequence is the continuation of the current tariff rather than a later agency-selected outcome.
classifications.evidence: I have determined that it is necessary and appropriate, at this time, to maintain the current tariff level as it applies to other countries.

classifications.rationale: The President presently amends the tariff schedule and establishes both an increased duty and a conditional exemption for qualifying Mexican steel products, directly determining their tariff treatment.
classifications.evidence: Imports of steel articles and derivative steel articles that are products of Mexico shall be exempt from the duty provided that such steel products are melted and poured in Mexico, Canada, or the United States.

classifications.rationale: The provision itself imposes a mandatory disclosure duty on importers to provide melt-and-pour origin information to CBP; the regulated parties' legal obligation arises from the proclamation.
classifications.evidence: importers of steel and steel derivative articles shall provide to CBP the information necessary to identify the countries where the steel used in the manufacture of steel articles imports, covered by clause 1 of Proclamation 9705, and derivative steel articles, specified in Annex II of Proclamation 9980, are melted and poured.

classifications.rationale: Although CBP is directed to implement information requirements, the segment also itself fixes when the HTSUS modifications become legally effective and declares their continuing duration.
classifications.evidence: The modifications to the HTSUS made by clause 1 of this proclamation shall be effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 10, 2024

classifications.rationale: The President directly prescribes the tariff treatment of specified Mexican steel imports upon entry after the stated time and supersedes inconsistent prior presidential provisions; the import consequence occurs under this segment itself.
classifications.evidence: shall be subject upon entry for consumption made on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 10, 2024, to the provisions of Proclamations 9894 and 9980.
